articles.title: Sara Duterte had over P10M in withdrawals, check encashment in Dec. 2024 -- AMLC witness
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte had over P10 million in over-the-counter withdrawals and check encashment in December 2024, Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura…

blocks.text: Published October 5, 2026 5:06pm

Vice President Sara Duterte had over P10 million in over-the-counter withdrawals and check encashment in December 2024, Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura testified Monday.
In his testimony during Day 33 of Duterte's impeachment trial, Buenaventura identified the following transactions:

items: P2.371 million in an over-the-counter withdrawal reported by Land Bank of the Philippines-San Pedro on December 5, 2024;
P1.7 million in a check encashment reported by Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co.-Davao/Ecoland on December 20, 2024; and
P5.969 million in a withdrawal reported by BDO Unibank Inc.-Davao Rizal on December 20, 2024.

blocks.text: The prosecution is presenting evidence for Article 2 of the impeachment case against Duterte, which alleges unexplained wealth stemming from her alleged failure to truthfully disclose assets in her SALNs and failure to divest from businesses as required of the President and Vice President under the Constitution.
“CWDLO means withdrawals over the counter... client's withdrawal from its deposit account through over the counter,” Buenaventura said, referring to an acronym in the AMLC report.
Private prosecutor Mae Divinagracia then asked Buenaventura how many days were left before the end of the year when the withdrawals were made.
“11 days, Your Honor,” Buenaventura replied.
Divinagracia then remarked, “11 days, just like the confidential fund."

She was alluding to the Office of the Vice President's (OVP) disbursement of P125 million in confidential funds in 2022 within 11 days, based on Commission on Audit records and the OVP's submission to state prosecutors.
Defense lawyer Mark Vinluan objected to Divinagracia's remark about the confidential funds and moved to strike it from the record.

Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero granted Vinluan's motion to strike Divinagracia's remark involving the confidential funds but allowed the prosecution to continue presenting evidence through Buenaventura.

On Day 25 of the impeachment trial, prosecution witness lawyer Karen Batu of the Office of the Ombudsman testified that Duterte did not declare cash on hand or cash in bank in her Statements of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALNs) from 2019 to 2025.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Impeachment court OKs presentation of dollar accounts in Sara Duterte trial
articles.summary: Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero on Monday denied the objection to present foreign currency-denominated accounts in the trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.

blocks.text: Published October 5, 2026 4:58pm
Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero on Monday denied the objection to present foreign currency-denominated accounts in the trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.

This was after Senator-Judge Imee Marcos objected to Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura, a witness presented by the House prosecution panel, reading details on a non-peso account during the trial.
“It’s very, very clear, well established in both the [former president] Erap [Estrada] and [former chief justice Renato] Corona impeachment that foreign currency accounts are excluded,” Marcos said.

Escudero, however, maintained in an extended ruling that the confidentiality afforded to foreign currency deposits does not exempt it from the reporting and inquiry provisions under Republic Act No. 9160 or the Anti-Money Laundering Act.

Citing Section 76(2) of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas’ Manual of Regulations on Foreign Exchange Transactions, the presiding officer said that the absolutely confidential nature of foreign currency deposits under the Foreign Currency Deposit Act shall not apply to a covered institution that reports foreign currency deposits in covered transaction reports or suspicious transaction reports to the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC), pursuant to Section 9(c) of Republic Act No. 9160, as amended.

“Thus, the suspicious transaction reports or covered transaction reports submitted to the AMLC do not acquire the status of absolute confidentiality merely because they contain information concerning foreign-currency deposit accounts,” Escudero said.

“In Republic of the Philippines v. Sandiganbayan, the Court ruled that the AMLC cannot invoke the confidentiality provisions under the AMLC to prevent disclosure of information on covered and suspicious transactions. The Court did not distinguish between peso and foreign-currency-denominated transactions,” he added.

Escudero also clarified that the impeachment court is not, at this point, compelling any bank or covered institution to disclose information concerning foreign-currency deposits maintained by the Vice President.
He said Buenaventura is only being asked to testify on records and financial information that are already in his lawful possession, through reports submitted by covered institutions to his office.
“The confidentiality of foreign currency deposits cannot operate to place information lawfully reported to the AMLC beyond the reach of the impeachment court,” the presiding officer said.

“A contrary interpretation would be untenable. While covered institutions are required to flag transactions regardless of currency denomination to the AMLC, and are, in that instance, exempt from the confidentiality provisions of the FCDA. The AMLC, despite being the government body legally authorized to receive and analyze those reports, would be prevented from explaining or authenticating lawfully acquired information before a competent tribunal,” he continued. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: Israel's mental health crisis in the wake of Oct. 7 attacks
articles.summary: More than a third of Israelis have shown symptoms of mental health conditions, a report found. Three years after the October 7 attack, the country's health system is still struggling to come to terms…

image.caption: Almost 400 people were murdered at the Nova festival in IsraelImage: Ronen Zvulun/REUTERS

blocks.text: Warning: This article contains references to death by suicide that some readers may find disturbing.
As October 7's third anniversary approaches, Ronen Shalev's body tells him something's coming.
"You start shivering," he tells DW. "It's not just one day and you move on. We have many graves to visit, many families to meet. It's a difficult time and you feel it in your body."

Both of his children attended the Nova Party in Israel's south, where almost 400 people were killed in a terrorist attack carried out by Palestinian militant group Hamas and its affiliates in Gaza. In total, roughly 1,200 people were killed in the attack and around 250 were taken hostage.
The attack triggered the war in Gaza, during which Israel has killed tens of thousands of Palestinians and displaced much of the territory's population.
Shalev's son, Roee, was shot and hospitalized, but he survived. Roee's partner, Mapal Adam, was killed in front of his eyes. Shalev's daughter, Lior, also made it out.
Shortly after that day, Shalev's wife Gavriela went missing, before her body was found in a burned car with a goodbye letter. "She couldn't handle the sorrow from that day," Shalev says.

At the same time, his son Roee's post-traumatic symptoms started emerging, mostly in the form of extreme mood swings. "He went to treatment to please me, but he didn't really believe in it. He thought he was OK, that he was strong," Shalev remembers.
Two years after Gavriela's death, Roee couldn't take it anymore, either.
"I'm alive, but I'm dead within," Roee wrote in his goodbye message, which he posted on his Instagram account. "I'm sorry."
A country in post-traumatic state
Since October 2023, Israel has been grappling with a mental health crisis of unprecedented scale.

According to a report by Israel's State Comptroller from February 2025, some 39% of the Israeli public reported suffering from post-traumatic symptoms, depression, anxiety or a combination of the three, on a medium or severe level.

This amounts to some 3 million people, 600,000 of whom could suffer severely. However, the report also found that the number of people receiving mental health treatment had only risen by 1% since October 7, 2023, a difference of around 60,000 people.
Among the affected groups are survivors of the attack, as well as people evacuated from their homes in Israel's south and north due to the war.

Noga Dagan-Buzaglo is a researcher with the Adva Center, a think tank focusing on inequality in Israeli society. She wrote an extensive paper about Israel's mental health system and its challenges post-October 7.
She tells DW that while the country's mental health budget did increase due to the war, it was too little, too late, as the health system faced an ongoing crisis that was not handled properly.
"The biggest challenge is convincing people to work in Israel's public mental health system, both due to lower wages in comparison to the private sector and due to an overload of work," she says.
Survivors mourn victims of October 7 music festival killings
Sedatives often the go-to solution

The current situation affects mental health professionals, too. Research by the University of Haifa found that 84% of the therapists who treated people affected by the October 7 attack showed traumatic symptoms themselves, and some 45% of them said they feel mentally exhausted.

Israel's Health Ministry has repeatedly said it has increased funding and job openings for the country's public mental health system, but staffing shortages remain, especially in peripheral regions in the far north and south.

Because of these issues, the report said waiting times for treatment through Israel's public healthcare system were longer than six months. In some cases, Dagan-Buzaglo says, patients had to wait more than a year before receiving help.

Mental health NGOs and volunteers try to fill the gaps, often struggling themselves under the workload. This also leads to an increased use of prescription medications. Some people turn to substances like alcohol and drugs.
The Israeli Ministry of Health said earlier this year that it had registered a rise of between 13% and 17% in the prescription of sedatives, sleep aids and antidepressants.

Those who suffer from the situation the most are the ones who cannot afford to pay a private therapist. Dagan-Buzaglo labels the Israeli public health system's response to the situation as "simply bad."

blocks.caption: Soldiers are one of the groups affected by Israel's mental health crisisImage: Avi Ohayon/REUTERS

blocks.text: Soldiers at risk
Combat soldiers have received a special focus when it comes to Israel's mental health crisis.

Statistics published by the Israeli parliament and the IDF suggest a sharp rise of suicide cases among reservists: from a maximum of one annual case in the six years preceding the war to 11 cases in 2024, as well as nine cases investigated as suspected suicides in 2025. This does not include ex-soldiers who committed suicide due to trauma after the end of their service.

Dagan-Buzaglo, a researcher at the Adva Center, says that while professionals receive better pay and conditions working for the army, the lack of personnel is still apparent. "In the army, too, the length and quality of treatment are by far not at an adequate level."

To start solving the problem for both civilians and soldiers, she believes the system needs more support. "We have to acknowledge the fact that trauma is not over after a year. This means investing money."
Breaking the taboo
Ronen Shalev holds regular lectures and talks about the importance of mental health, often to groups of soldiers. He believes this is the best way to continue his son's legacy of fighting to live on.
Shalev, who himself was diagnosed with post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), says he made a choice to live his life to its fullest.

His message: The taboo regarding suicidality — which still exists across Israeli society — needs to be broken. "This is especially true regarding those who say they are strong. They're the scary ones as they're less likely to receive treatment."
For Shalev, speaking publicly about his family's experience has become part of his own recovery — and a way to encourage others to seek help before they reach a crisis point.
"Life, with all its pain, is still worth deciding in favor of," he said.
October 7 survivors recall attacks on Kibbutz Nir Oz

If you are suffering from serious emotional strain or suicidal thoughts, do not hesitate to seek professional help. You can find information on where to find such help, no matter where you live in the world, at this website: https://befrienders.org/

articles.title: China rejects Trillanes claims on funds linked to Duterte groups
articles.summary: The embassy called allegations of funneling funds to a local faction a "false narrative."

blocks.text: Former senator Antonio Trillanes IV presents financial transactions allegedly involving Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband Manases Carpio during a press conference yesterday.
The STAR / Miguel De Guzman
MANILA, Philippines — The Chinese Embassy in Manila denied allegations that Beijing funneled funds to a Philippine political faction, dismissing the claims as a "false narrative."
In a statement on Monday, October 5, Chinese Embassy spokesperson Ji Lingpeng said certain Philippine politicians had fabricated and spread the allegation.
He also said the embassy's official website had been maliciously linked as a redirect destination to support the claims.

"The Chinese Embassy in the Philippines has noted that recently certain Philippine politicians fabricated and spread a false narrative alleging that China had funneled funds to a particular political faction in the Philippines, and the Embassy's website has been maliciously linked as a redirect destination," Ji said.
Ji urged Philippine politicians to stop what he described as political manipulation and refrain from dragging domestic politics into relations between Manila and Beijing.

"Attempts to achieve personal political gains by smearing and discrediting China and harming China's interests and image are doomed to fail, and will ultimately undermine the interests of the Philippines and its people," Ji said.
He also warned that the embassy would take measures to protect what it described as its legitimate interests and dignity.

The embassy did not name the politicians or political faction referred to in its statement. But the denial came days after former Sen. Antonio Trillanes IV alleged that more than P319 million from Chinese government and corporate sources went to CALE88 Foods Corp., a company linked to Vice President Sara Duterte's husband, Manases Carpio.
Trillanes also alleged that P150 million from the Chinese Embassy went to the Tapang at Malasakit Alliance for the Philippines, an organization associated with Duterte.
Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro earlier urged Trillanes to turn over any evidence to law enforcement authorities, saying the allegations could have national security implications if substantiated.

articles.title: Israel observes October 7 anniversary with national memorial day
articles.summary: Israel is holding memorial ceremonies nationwide for those killed in the October 7, 2023 Hamas terror attacks and soldiers who died in the ensuing war.

image.caption: The Hamas terror attacks on October 7, 2023, resulted in over 1,200 deaths and sparked nearly three years of an ongoing Israeli military campaign in Gaza [FILE: October 7, 2025]Image: Ahmad Gharabli/AFP

blocks.text: Israelis observing a national memorial day on Monday for those killed in the October 7, 2023 Hamas terror attacks and the soldiers who died in the Gaza war, Israeli media reported.

Two state ceremonies are being held at Mount Herzl in Jerusalem, where President Isaac Herzog, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and other senior officials are expected to attend, The Jerusalem Post reported.
More memorial events, rallies and ceremonies are planned across the country with schools, municipalities and communities also holding events throughout the day.

Flags at state institutions, police stations, prisons and military bases were lowered to half-mast, reports said. The memorial fell on October 5 this year due to the Hebrew calendar, which is lunisolar.
October 7 terror attacks set of chain of events

The Hamas terror attack on October 7 killed some 1,200 people in Israel, with the Palestinian militant also taking another 251 hostages into Gaza. It was the single deadliest day for Jewish people since the Holocaust.
The October 7, 2023, attacks had massive consequences not only for Israeli society but also for Palestinians in Gaza, where Hamas had maintained power since the territory last held elections in 2006.

Following the Hamas attacks, the Israeli military began a war targeting Hamas in Gaza. The European Union, as well as the United States, Germany, and other countries, classify Hamas as a terrorist organization.
Israel's war on Hamas left more than 73,650 Palestinians dead in Gaza , most of them civilians, according to Gaza's Health Ministry.

articles.title: FACT CHECK: Congress did not vote on any new impeachment case vs Marcos
articles.summary: The dismissed impeachment complaints in February granted Marcos a one-year immunity from any new impeachment proceedings

blocks.text: Claim: Forty-six lawmakers from the House of Representatives voted to impeach President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. at the height of Vice President Sara Duterte’s own impeachment trial.
Why we fact-checked this: Facebook user Boss Onin posted a video reacting to a supposed news card announcing an alleged impeachment complaint against Marcos.
The card read, “46 congressman bumoto sa impeachment ni BBM.” (46 congressmen voted for BBM’s impeachment.)
The Facebook user then said, “Ito na yung kinakatakutan ng mga loyalista (This is what the loyalists have been dreading).”
The user made two reaction videos out of it, with one having 2 million views as of this posting. Combined, the video of the claim reached 2.5 million views, had 49,900 comments, and 34,000 shares.
Commenters echoed the sentiment and called for the President’s impeachment.
The facts: No active impeachment complaint is lodged against Marcos as of September. There is also no House justice committee hearing discussing any impeachment case as of this posting.

However, two impeachment complaints were filed in January that accused him of violating the Constitution, graft and corruption, and betrayal of public trust. They were later dismissed in February due to lack of substance.

The first complaint, filed by lawyer Andre De Jesus and endorsed by Representative Jett Nisay, had sought Marcos’ removal for allowing the arrest of former president Rodrigo Duterte by the International Criminal Court, his alleged drug use, and his supposed role in the flood control scandal. Forty-two lawmakers voted to dismiss it.

Three Makabayan bloc members filed the second complaint, which focused on Marcos supposedly orchestrating systemic corruption involving unprogrammed appropriations and kickbacks. Thirty-nine lawmakers voted to junk the complaint.
Rappler has previously debunked another Marcos impeachment claim that repackaged a clip from a House justice committee hearing and made it look like a recent news update.
The dismissed complaints granted Marcos one year of immunity from any new impeachment proceedings, based on the Constitution. Complainants cannot file another case against him until January 2027.
Impeachment trial: The false claim surfaced at the height of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial.
While Marcos’ impeachment cases were ruled to have no sufficient substance, the House saw probable cause in Duterte’s case, leading to her second impeachment.
A Supreme Court ruling halted the impeachment proceedings in July 2025 and granted Duterte a one-year impeachment immunity. She was impeached again in May 2026.
The Senate has currently convened as an impeachment court to try the Vice President. The trial enters its 33rd day on Monday, October 5.
Previous fact checks: Rappler has debunked numerous false claims involving Marcos:

items: FACT CHECK: Jonvic Remulla did not say Marcoses are ‘sure to be jailed’ after 2028
FACT CHECK: Marcos did not say he wants another 6-year presidential term
FACT CHECK: Claire Castro quote on Marcos’ plans to run for VP is fake
FACT CHECK: Video of Marcos saying Romualdez’s arrest is ‘staged’ is AI-generated
FACT CHECK: Video of Marcos and Romualdez laughing about ‘fooling’ the public is AI-generated

blocks.text: – Eirene Manatlao/Rappler.com

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

articles.title: 13 alleged True Brown Style members arrested in Metro Manila since 2024
articles.summary: Police said the suspects were linked to 21 alleged violations and are stepping up efforts to prevent the recruitment and grooming of minors.

blocks.text: Photos showing policemen of the NCRPO.
STAR / Ernie Penaredondo

MANILA, Philippines — The National Capital Region Police Office arrested 13 individuals allegedly linked to the True Brown Style (TBS) group in operations conducted from August 2024 to September 28, 2026.
In a statement Monday, October 5, the NCRPO said two suspects were arrested in 2024, four in 2025 and seven in the first nine months of 2026.
Six were arrested under the Southern Police District, four under the Manila Police District, two under the Quezon City Police District and one under the Northern Police District.

Police said the 13 individuals were linked to 21 alleged violations, including four firearms offenses, three illegal gambling cases, three kidnapping or illegal detention cases and two drug-related offenses.
Other alleged violations involved theft, homicide, trafficking in persons, cybercrime, the Anti-Hazing Law, child abuse, grave coercion and resistance or disobedience to a person in authority.
Focus on recruitment of minors

Police Brigadier General Christopher Abrahano, the NCRPO's officer-in-charge, ordered police districts and units across Metro Manila to intensify intelligence gathering and operations against people linked to the group.
A particular focus is to monitor operations that recruit minors.

"Our children should never be used as tools for criminal activities," Abrahano said. "We will pursue those who exploit children and ensure that our young people are protected from criminal influence."
The NCRPO also directed police districts to strengthen coordination with local governments, schools, barangays, parents and community leaders to identify possible recruitment involving minors.
Abrahano said the campaign would go beyond arrests, with police also monitoring recruitment patterns and coordinating with government agencies on intervention and rehabilitation for affected minors.
He urged parents, teachers, guardians and the public to report information involving the alleged grooming, exploitation or recruitment of minors for criminal activities.

Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla earlier described TBS as a community-based criminal group with a presence in Metro Manila and many provinces. He said most members are in their late teens and early 20s and alleged that the group recruits children as young as 14 or 15 for criminal activities.
Remulla also alleged that some initiation rites involve robbing convenience stores at gunpoint.
"Before you can join the group, you have to rob a convenience store at gunpoint," Remulla previously told reporters.
Authorities have said they are gathering intelligence on the group's membership and structure as part of efforts to stop its alleged recruitment of minors.

articles.title: AMLC: Sara Duterte, husband had P4.4B in covered, suspicious bank transactions
articles.summary: At least P4.4 billion worth of covered and suspicious transactions were recorded under the bank accounts of Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio, Anti-Money Laundering Council…

blocks.text: Published October 5, 2026 4:26pm

At least P4.4 billion worth of covered and suspicious transactions were recorded under the bank accounts of Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband, Manases Carpio, Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) Executive Director Ronel Buenaventura said Monday.

The value was reduced from P6.7 billion, that Buenaventura testified to in the House justice panel, to P4.4 billion after a correction was made by one of the subject banks, BPI, as communicated to the Senate court by private prosecutor Mae Divinagracia.

Back in April, Buenaventura also told the House committee on justice that at least 18 of the transactions cited in the affidavit of former senator Antono Trillanes IV submitted to the House committee on justice correspond to entries in AMLC records, including three transactions allegedly involving supposed drug personality Samuel “Sammy” Uy.
The 18 transactions confirmed by Buenaventura were randomly selected by House Senior Deputy Minority Leader Leila de Lima of the ML party-list.
Of the 18 transactions, Buenaventura said three were deposited in batches amounting to P7.4 million each in March 2011, October 2011, and April 2012.

However, Buenaventura clarified that the AMLC cannot confirm whether such three batches of transfers came from Uy as it only monitors transactions reported by covered institutions and not direct ownership of accounts.

Buenaventura also told the House justice panel that the Vice President was the subject of 27 suspicious transaction reports submitted by covered institutions from August 2024 to January 2026 concerning suspected drug trafficking, graft and corruption, and malversation of public funds and property.

The AMLC said the reports were triggered by references to the House Quad Committee hearings on the Duterte administration’s war on drugs, news reports alleging involvement of the Vice President’s husband Manases in the 2017 P6.4-billion shabu shipment, the 2025 impeachment complaint against Duterte, and alleged misuse of confidential and intelligence funds. —AOL, GMA News
